limits: 20ms accounting windows and 200ms PSS samples are not arbitrary instantaneous peaks.
Observed helper count is a lower bound; very short helpers can finish between samples.
Cgroup CPU includes helpers; proc child ticks are quantized and cannot exactly split short helper cost.
The observer is excluded from Guard cgroups but still consumes guest CPU.
Common generic base/host libraries are controlled; this is not a comparison of two different installed tool bundles.
Two repetitions per variant are small samples, not confidence intervals or a hardware guarantee.
No overall CPU/RAM reduction is claimed; steady-state mean CPU slightly increased within overlapping trial ranges.
Current recovery PSS maxima include a sampled short-lived helper; baseline maximum snapshots include only three controllers. PSS sampling does not establish either true instantaneous maximum.
memory.peak is per-cgroup lifetime high-water, not a simultaneous aggregate; no addition of independent peaks is used.
Whole-experiment application maxima include later observation/audit activity; fault-overlap maxima are separately reported.
PSS, cgroup accounting and RAM toolkit file sizes are different accounting domains and cannot be added to infer whole-machine RAM.
Logger, observer, application load and kernel workers are outside the Guard cgroup aggregation.
